Cytochrome P450

One axiom, two constants, seventeen papers.

A partition-depth account of enzyme catalysis — and an honest report on what it has and has not shown.

kundai sachikonye · 3 August 2026

Start with a claim everybody has heard

Infinite monkeys, infinite typewriters, eventually Hamlet.

It is worth doing the arithmetic. A QWERTY keyboard has 47 keys. Hamlet is roughly 130,000 characters.

47⁻¹³⁰·⁰⁰⁰

probability of the sequence

10⁻²¹⁷·⁰⁰⁰

which is to say

Give every atom in the observable universe — 10⁸⁰ of them — a typewriter, and one keystroke per Planck time, for the age of the universe.

Still short by 216,860 orders of magnitude. The thought experiment does not nearly fail. It fails by a margin that has no physical referent.

Plymouth University actually ran it in 2003. Six macaques, one keyboard, one month. The output consisted almost entirely of the letter S.

The mistake is not the arithmetic

The calculation assumes the monkey samples uniformly from key-space, and that Shakespeare somehow does not.

The monkey is not random; the monkey is doing what monkeys do. The human is not magical; the human is doing what humans do. Neither is sampling from key-space. Each is evaluating a receiver.

monograph introduction, §1

Once you say that, the search space was never there to be searched. It was an artefact of insisting on a uniform measure over a space neither party inhabits.

And the same move applies to a problem in this room's actual literature.

Levinthal's paradox is the same shape

the enumeration

CYP3A4 is 503 residues. Three conformational states each.

10²⁴⁰

configurations

The protein folds in milliseconds.

the evaluation

The receiver resolves the fold in six categorical steps — log₃ 503 ≈ 5.69, rounded up.

6

steps

Not a faster search. A different question.

The reduction from 10²⁴⁰ to six is not a clever search algorithm. It is the dissolution of the search frame.

One axiom, two calibrated constants

Bounded phase space — Vol(Ω) < ∞ — therefore a finite number of distinguishable states, N = Vol(Ω)/hⁿ. Everything else follows.

k        =  ν_floor · exp(−ΔM)          universal rate law
M        =  Σ log_b(k_i)                partition depth
S_P      =  k_B · M · ln b              depth ≡ entropy

ν_floor  =  10¹⁰ s⁻¹     ħ/k_BT ≈ 25 fs, damped by solvent (κ ≈ 2.5×10⁻⁴)
T_part   =  65 kJ/mol    partition temperature

Two numbers, calibrated once. Not re-fitted per paper, per isoform, or per reaction. Every rate in the monograph is that law with a different ΔM.

A law with no free parameters

log₁₀(k_cat/K_M) ≈ 10 − d_C

Where d_C counts the distinct categorical layers a substrate must cross. No fitted parameters at all.

enzymed_Cpredictedmeasured
superoxide dismutase110⁹ M⁻¹s⁻¹7×10⁹
chymotrypsin410⁶1.7×10⁶
NADPH→FAD→FMN→heme410⁶~10⁶

Diffusion-limited enzymes are the d_C = 1 case, which is why they cluster where they do. That was not put in by hand.

The catalytic cycle as a closed orbit

The seven-state P450 cycle, with each transition read as a partition-depth cost ΔM. The orbit closes: state 7 releases product and returns to state 1.

Compound I is licensed, not explained away

O–O heterolysis at ΔM = ln 2 exactly. The species is locally the least feasible point on the orbit — which is why it took until 2010 to trap.

Four numbers, no fitting. These four are the reason I think there is something here — and I will now tell you about the ones that do not work.

The piece I am most confident in

The receiver addresses states by partition coordinates (n, ℓ, m, s), with capacity C(n) = 2n² — which reproduces 2, 8, 18, 32 without being told to.

s_orbital

Topologically conserved. Fixed by π₁(SO(3)) = Z₂ — not a dynamical choice.

s_state

Receiver-internal and free. This is what moves during spin-crossover.

So the low-spin → high-spin transition on substrate binding is reorganisation within a categorical cell, not a transition between cells. The selection rules Δℓ = ±1, |Δm| ≤ 1 are then topological rather than postulated.

What the 140 validation scripts actually check

Seventeen papers, 140 scripts, 142 result files, all passing. Here is what a typical check contains.

# from construction/membrane-cofactor-cpr/.../03_fmn_heme_distance.json
k_ET_exp        = 5.0e6        # measured, from the literature
ΔM_ET           = ln(ν_floor / k_ET_exp) = 7.6009
k_reconstructed = ν_floor · exp(−ΔM_ET)  = 5.0e6

"k_ET_reconstructed_matches": true

That is exp(ln(x)) = x. It cannot fail. ΔM is a re-parameterisation of rate, so a check of this shape verifies my algebra, not my physics.

What the suites do establish: the same two constants are applied consistently across seventeen papers with no cross-paper contradiction. That is worth having. It is not empirical confirmation, and I would rather say so than have you find it.

Four things wrong with it that I know about

defectstatus
Closed-orbit paper says 'sub-nanosecond return'. Its own JSON says 1.51 ns.A 1000× unit slip, six occurrences. The JSON is right; the prose is wrong.
Abstract quotes a 1040× ratio where the cycle-level 132× belongs.Conclusion survives. The number does not.
The aliphatic KIE appears as 7.2, 9.63 and 7.7 in three papers.All inside the experimental 4–11 window, so all three passed. That is a test that is too loose.
Compound I potential: 0.9 V in one abstract, 0.53 V in its own proof.Unreconciled.

The KIE one is the instructive failure. Three different values all passed because the acceptance window was the experimental range, which is wide. A test that admits everything tests nothing.

One number here is a prediction, not a re-parameterisation

The kinetic isotope effect should fall with temperature by a specific factor.

9.63

predicted KIE at 310 K

7.63

predicted KIE at 350 K

1.26×

the discriminating quantity

Direction is not the claim — every semiclassical account has KIE falling with T, because exp(ΔZPE/kᵇT) is decreasing in T. Saying otherwise would be overclaiming, and an earlier version of this slide did.

The claim is magnitude. Tunnelling-corrected QM/MM predicts a steeper fall, since the tunnelling contribution decays as temperature rises. Mine is the bare zero-point term. The two diverge over a 40 K window on a measurement that is standard, cheap, and already runs on automated screening hardware.

If the fall is steeper than 1.26×, my treatment is missing the tunnelling temperature-dependence — which it is, and I know where. One afternoon of instrument time settles it.

The monograph runs

Each paper is also a program. Eleven lessons, one language, one receiver whose state accumulates down the ladder.

-- 04_catalytic-cycle.shk
receiver bio
floor 3.7e-4                      -- nothing is free

O2    := substrate "O2"
cycle := track O2 in E
           with reps mass, charge, spin
           until converge
           yield amalgamation

observe cycle
-- 7 states, 8 transitions, ΣΔM = 4.963, orbit closed

Heavy verbs replay the paper's validated numbers rather than recomputing them — the interpreter says so in its header. It is a teaching surface, not a solver.

live

What this does not do

not thiswhy
It is not a docking or structure-prediction tool.It gives an address, not coordinates. It will not tell you where a ligand sits.
It does not replace QM/MM.It has no electronic-structure content. Where QM/MM computes, this re-parameterises.
The validation is not empirical confirmation.Named on the earlier slide. Internal consistency across seventeen papers, no more.
The database-recovery accuracy is not measured on sequences.It is derived from a bit ratio. The Shannon arithmetic is sound; the label 'accuracy' overstates it.

Why this belongs near a robot

The prediction that discriminates is a temperature series — the tedious kind of measurement.

  • KIE across 310–350 K, deuterated and protiated substrate, one enzyme. Tedious by hand; unattended on a screening platform.
  • The receiver is the same object across seventeen papers — one address space for sequence, fold, isoform, and variant. That is a schema an automated pipeline can carry.
  • Every claim above resolves to a number in a JSON file next to the paper that makes it. Including the ones that are wrong.

I would rather bring you a framework with four known defects and one falsifiable prediction than a clean one with neither.
